trust_decision.summary: Two decisions are made by this fix: (1) whether an incoming RPC is authorized or the process panics, decided when RBAC policy protos are converted to matchers (unsupported rule types are silently dropped, and not_rule/not_id index mList[0] without a non-empty check); (2) whether a peer can queue unbounded control frames, decided by whether each cbItem counts toward the control buffer's throttle threshold.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names xDS RBAC first, and this is where the authorization decision is materialized: rule types the package comments declare 'not supported ... no-op' are dropped, and not_rule builds notMatcher from mList[0] with no length check, so an unsupported inner rule is a fail-open/permission widening or an index-out-of-range panic.

xDS RBAC HTTP filter config and authz.NewStatic / authz.NewFileWatcher

xDS RBAC HTTP filter config (new requested_server_name matcher)
grpc.Server.Serve (server.go:1033 -> transport.NewServerTransport) and grpc ClientConn (clientconn.go:1527 -> transport.NewHTTP2Client)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT is only an optional escape hatch (the fix's own comment says it will be removed in v1.83.0), so a solver can argue the limit is enforced by the default constant in controlbuf.go and skip the env-config package entirely.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Outgoing HEADERS and DATA frames must stay exempt from the control-buffer throttle or a large response / bidirectional stream stalls the reader and deadlocks; the fix adds TestControlBuffer_NoThrottleForNonThrottledItems for exactly this. A second legitimate value next to the RBAC sink: requested_server_name must keep matching "" and source_ip must stay equivalent to direct_remote_ip per A41, so a blanket error on every 'unsupported' type breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: control-buffer item kind: PING, SETTINGS, RST_STREAM, WINDOW_UPDATE, GOAWAY, registerStream, earlyAbortStream, closeConnection, outFlowControlSizeRequest are throttled; HEADERS and DATA are exempt
server-side HandleStreams reader vs client-side reader (both gate on controlBuffer.throttle)
RBAC permission rule oneof: and_rules, or_rules, any, header, url_path, destination_ip, destination_port, not_rule, metadata (invert true/false), requested_server_name, and unknown-typed rules
RBAC principal identifier oneof: and_ids, or_ids, any, authenticated, direct_remote_ip, header, url_path, not_id, source_ip, remote_ip, metadata (invert true/false), and unknown-typed identifiers
not_rule / not_id wrapping a single unsupported rule vs an and/or set mixing supported and unsupported children
requested_server_name string matcher: exact "" (must match) vs exact "foo" (must not match)
source_ip CidrRange: address inside vs outside the prefix, and an unparseable prefix (must error)
GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT: unset, below min, above max 10000, non-numeric

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new peer-driven control item type that does not embed throttledItem / returns isThrottled()==false
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the buffer already has 14 item types and each new HTTP/2 feature adds one; nothing in the type system forces a new item to be counted

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new Envoy permission or principal rule case that is appended as a no-op (the pre-fix metadata/requested_server_name pattern)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Envoy keeps adding rule types and gRPC tracks A41 incrementally, so a copy-pasted no-op case is a natural maintainer mistake

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a router/override RBAC filter path that builds matchers without the fail-closed conversion
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: RBACPerRoute override parsing already exists as a second config route and is parsed by the same untrusted-proto entry point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a client-side mirror of a server frame handler whose item bypasses the throttle accounting
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the client transport already mirrors the server's handleWindowUpdate/handleData controlBuf puts

O9_family: incorrect authorization / fail-open policy conversion (CWE-863), uncaught panic (CWE-248), and unbounded control-frame buffering / resource exhaustion (CWE-770)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 (go.mod:3); standard go build/test, no cgo required for these packages
O10_build.project_tests: internal/transport/transport_test.go and keepalive_test.go (transport behaviour; defaultTestShortTimeout at keepalive_test.go:48), internal/xds/rbac/rbac_engine_test.go (TestNewChainEngine, TestChainEngine), authz/grpc_authz_end2end_test.go (static policy interceptor e2e); the fix adds internal/transport/controlbuf_test.go and new rbac_engine_test.go cases (both absent at the pin).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add only the frame type named in the report (WINDOW_UPDATE) to isTransportResponseFrame and raise the 50 constant, leaving earlyAbortStream, registerStream, cleanupStream with rst=false, incomingGoAway and outgoingWindowUpdate uncounted, and/or reject every unsupported RBAC rule type outright, breaking requested_server_name and source_ip support.

out_of_scope_notes: scripts/vet.sh:200-201 - the fix adds GetSourceIp to the unused-generated-method ignore list; tooling only, not a security fix site.
